Key Takeaways


##


1. Audit your online presence before Q4 to identify website, marketing, and customer experience gaps.
2. Keep business listings accurate and consistent to improve local business visibility and make it easier for customers to find you.
3. Build review momentum now so your business has fresh customer feedback when holiday shoppers start searching.
4. Use automation for repetitive follow-up, including lead nurturing, appointment reminders, and review requests.
5. Organize and segment customer contacts so your fall and holiday marketing reaches the right audiences with more relevant messages.
6. Prepare for AI-powered search by keeping your business information, website content, and reviews clear, accurate, and consistent across the web.


September is the calm before the holiday rush for many small businesses. It is also one of your last good opportunities to make improvements before fall demand picks up.


Instead of waiting until your calendar fills up, use September to get your marketing, customer experience, and operations ready for a busier Q4.


A strong[online presence](https://www.thryv.com/blog/spring-cleaning-your-online-presence-checklist-for-small-businesses/) management strategy can help you do that. When your website, listings, reviews, marketing, and customer communications are working together, it becomes easier for customers to find your business, decide to contact you, and stay connected after they do.


Use this September business growth checklist to identify what needs attention now, before the holiday rush begins.


## Your September Business Growth Checklist


- Audit your website and marketing performance
- Refresh your listings and local search presence
- Build review momentum before holiday shoppers arrive
- Automate lead nurturing and customer follow-up
- Clean up your CRM and segment holiday audiences


You do not have to tackle everything at once. Start with the area that has the biggest gap and work your way through the list.


## **1. Audit Your Website and Marketing Performance**


Before increasing your holiday marketing, take a look at how your current strategy is performing.


Your website, search presence, social media, advertising, and email campaigns all contribute to your online presence. But if you do not know which channels are bringing in traffic, leads, and customers, it is difficult to know where to invest more during Q4.


Start with a quick website and marketing audit.


### **Check your website**


Ask yourself:


- Is your business information current?
- Are your products and services clearly explained?
- Can customers easily call, book, request a quote or make a purchase?
- Are your calls to action easy to find?
- Does your website work well on mobile devices?
- Are your seasonal offers easy to find?
- Does the site clearly explain what makes your business different?


Your website is often one of the first places customers go after discovering your business. It should make it easy for them to understand what you offer and take the next step.


### **Review your marketing**


Look at your recent performance across:


- Organic search
- Paid advertising
- Social media
- Email and text campaigns
- Website traffic
- Lead generation
- Customer conversions


Then ask a simple question: **What should I do more of in Q4?**


You may find that one channel is consistently generating leads while another is taking time without producing much return. That insight can help you focus your holiday budget and time where they are most likely to make a difference.


[Reporting software](https://www.thryv.com/features/reporting-center/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) can help bring marketing performance into one place, making it easier to see what is driving activity and where you may need to make adjustments.


September Quick Win


Search your business name online and visit your website as if you were a new customer. Look for anything that could create friction or make it harder to contact you.


## **2. Refresh Your Listings and Local Search Presence**


Holiday customers are not only searching for what to buy. They are searching for **where to buy it** .


That makes accurate business listings an important part of online presence management and local business visibility.

There is another reason to pay attention to your digital presence before the holidays: **AI visibility** .


Customers are increasingly using AI-powered search tools to discover businesses, compare options, and get recommendations. Your business information needs to be clear and consistent enough for those systems to understand what you do, where you operate, and who you serve.

Start with the fundamentals:

## **3. Build Review Momentum Before Holiday Shoppers Arrive**


When customers are comparing businesses, reviews can help them decide which one to trust.


That makes September a good time to build your review momentum instead of waiting until holiday traffic is already coming in.


Look for natural opportunities to ask satisfied customers for feedback, such as after:


- Completing a service
- Finishing a project
- Delivering an order
- Completing an appointment
- Successfully resolving a customer issue


The key is consistency. Rather than relying on someone to remember to ask for a review, build the request into your normal customer process.


Automating review requests can make that easier.[Automated review tools](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organicsocial#ai-review-response) can send review requests after a sale while also helping businesses monitor and respond to reviews.


[Reviews can also support your visibility](https://www.thryv.com/blog/why-reviews-matter-for-ai-search/) beyond traditional search. Customer feedback can provide authentic language about your business, services, and location that helps potential customers understand what you offer.


And responding matters, too. A thoughtful response shows prospective customers that your business pays attention to its customers, not just its star rating.


**September quick win:** Identify the point in your customer journey when someone is most satisfied with your service and make that your standard moment for requesting a review.


## **4. Automate Lead Nurturing and Customer Follow-Up**


More holiday demand can mean more leads.


It can also mean more[opportunities for follow-up](https://www.thryv.com/blog/lead-response-time/) to get lost.


When your team is busy answering calls, serving customers, and managing day-to-day operations, remembering every follow-up can become difficult. Automation can help keep important communications moving without requiring someone to manually manage every interaction.


Consider automating:


**New lead follow-up:** Send a timely email or text after someone submits an inquiry.


**Appointment reminders:** Give customers a reminder before their scheduled appointment.


**Post-purchase follow-up:** Check in after a product or service has been delivered.


**Review requests:** Automatically ask customers to share their experience.


**Seasonal campaigns:** Send relevant promotions to specific customer groups based on their relationship with your business.


The goal is not to automate every customer interaction. It is to automate the repetitive steps, so your team can spend more time on the conversations that actually need a person.

## **5. Clean Up Your CRM and Segment Your Holiday Audiences**


Your CRM can become especially valuable during the holiday season, but only if the information inside it is organized.


Before you start your fall and holiday campaigns, take some time to clean up your contacts.


Start by:


- Removing duplicate contacts
- Updating outdated information
- Reviewing lead and customer statuses
- Identifying inactive contacts
- Checking that important customer details are complete
- Organizing contacts into useful segments


Then consider how different groups might respond to different messages.


For example:


**New leads** may need more information before they are ready to buy.


**Returning customers** may respond well to a loyalty offer.


**Past customers** may need a reminder about a seasonal product or service.


**High-value customers** may appreciate an exclusive promotion or early access.


**Inactive customers** may respond to a reason to come back.


Segmentation helps you move away from sending the same promotion to everyone and toward more relevant customer communication.


It also connects back to the bigger goal of[online presence management](https://www.thryv.com/features/local-listings/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organicsocial) . Your online presence is not just what customers see when they find you. It includes what happens after they become a lead or customer.


With your contacts, marketing, and customer interactions organized in one place, it becomes easier to create a consistent experience from first discovery through repeat business.


September quick win


Create three customer segments you can realistically use for your fall and holiday campaigns.

## **Get Your Online Presence Ready Before the Rush**


The holiday season does not have to be a scramble.


September gives you time to strengthen the foundation that supports your business when demand increases: your website, listings, reviews, follow-up processes, and customer data.


A stronger approach to online presence management can help you improve your online presence, strengthen local business visibility, build AI visibility, and create more opportunities to turn searches into customers.


You do not have to fix everything at once.


Start with the biggest gap. Make one improvement this week. Then move to the next.


By the time the holiday rush arrives, you will not just be reacting to more customers. You will have a stronger system in place to help you find them, follow up with them, and keep them coming back.
